```{r, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
options(highcharter.google_fonts = FALSE)
```

## A map from local GeoJSON

The package includes the state boundaries in `usgeojson`. Join its `name`
property to a column of state names. The values below are the percentage of
the population living in urban areas in the 1973 USArrests data.

```{r local-map}
states <- transform(USArrests, state = rownames(USArrests))
urban_map <- highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_add_series_map(usgeojson, states, value = "UrbanPop",
                    joinBy = c("name", "state"), name = "Urban population (%)") |>
  hc_title(text = "Urban population by state, 1973") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
urban_map
```

For a categorized choropleth, use the same chart and pass limits and
names to `hc_colorAxis()`. This groups states by their urban population share.

```{r categorized-map}
urban_map |>
  hc_colorAxis(dataClasses = list(
    list(to = 49, name = "Under 50%"),
    list(from = 50, to = 69, name = "50–69%"),
    list(from = 70, name = "70% and over")
  ))
```

## Projection and initial view

Use longitude first and latitude second. The two cities below have geographic
coordinates, so the map view can project the same points at different zoom
levels. The chart resizes with its container.

```{r mapview-cities}
cities <- list(list(name = "Santiago", lon = -70.67, lat = -33.45),
               list(name = "Valparaíso", lon = -71.62, lat = -33.05))
highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_add_series(type = "mappoint", data = cities, name = "Cities") |>
  hc_mapView(projection = list(name = "WebMercator"), center = c(-71.1, -33.3), zoom = 7) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

Use `mapline` for boundaries, `mapbubble` for locations with a magnitude,
`geoheatmap` for gridded geographic values and `flowmap` for connections.
The [series gallery](../series-gallery.html#mapline) contains runnable charts
for each of these types.

## Downloaded maps and web tiles

`hcmap()` reads the Highcharts map collection. This example needs network
access. Alternatively, download a GeoJSON once, keep it with the project
and pass it as `mapData` to a map series.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
hcmap("countries/nz/nz-all") |>
  hc_mapView(zoom = 3) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

A tiled web map requests tiles from its provider when the user pans or zooms.
For an offline report, use local boundaries or local tiles. The gallery uses
an embedded demonstration tile. For a live basemap:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_mapView(center = c(-70.67, -33.45), zoom = 9) |>
  hc_add_series(type = "tiledwebmap", provider = list(type = "OpenStreetMap"))
```

[Highcharts Maps documentation](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/maps/getting-started)
